newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Crude Outlook - Ample supply weighs on prices.
newsitem.headline: Asia Crude Outlook - Ample supply weighs on prices.

text.p: Asian crude oil prices are expected to see little respite this week from the bearish trend that has dogged the market for several weeks, traders said on Monday.
The Asian market has an overhang of crude, most noticeably Middle East barrels, displaced by large scale regional imports of West African oil.
The biggest loser has been light Middle East grades, with only a handful of Abu Dhabi crude traded so far for June.
"There is still a lot of crude out there," one trader said.
"The amount of West African coming this way will lighten the Asian refinery slate, so refiners won't need light Middle East grades," a trader said.
Oman crude has slumped to MPM -20 cents, with deals done late last week at -21, -20 and -19 cents after May traded only as low as MPM -4/-5 cents.
The weakness has largely been the result of the Oman/Dubai differential coming in a paltry five cents to +$1.00 for June, where as other grades saw a much stronger narrowing against the benchmark.
Traders said however that Oman might not see too much downside from current levels this week, although there were still several cargoes available to buyers.
"I don't think it will fall much further, but it is not exactly strong," one trader said.
However, "if potential buyers do not surface, it will go lower again. There are a lot of sellers out there. It could stabilize for a while, but it still has the potential to go lower," a trader said.
Most Dubai trade has been completed for June, which might offer the Middle East market some support.
A flurry of trades ahead of the Indian June crude oil tender award at the weekend, by traders fearing that India might not award Dubai for the second month running, tightened the market.
Late last week the June/July Dubai spread moved to a single-digit backwardation after falling into contango in recent weeks. On Monday it was assessed at +3/+10 cents.
However, India awarded three Dubai cargoes in the tender to British Petroleum at first-half quotes flat, and two cargoes to trader Phibro at flat and minus two cents.
Traders estimated that only a few, if any, cargoes were available for spot trade.
Minas and Duri were still trying to shrug off an overhang of supply, although Minas appeared in better shape that Duri, market sources said.
Traders said 200,000 barrels of Minas traded on Friday in Japan at ICP +10/15 cents, was in line with recent deals.
Traders said they expected the market to remain at latest traded levels for the rest of May.
"The Minas market is pretty balanced," one trader said. "There are about 500,000 barrels left, which is not a big amount."
He said Minas equity sellers could absorb the remaining barrels, or roll them forward into June, if they felt prices could weaken again which would underpin the market.
But Duri was weak, valued around ICP -20 cents, with barrels overhanging the market. A South Korean refiner bid at ICP -40 cents on Friday.
However, the downside could be limited, traders said.
"Most of the sellers are not worried. Many of the fuel oil tenders have not picked up blending stock, so sellers will hope there will be second half May demand," a trader said.
Malaysian Tapis crude appeared to have established a floating rate against Tapis swaps of plus 40 cents after Petronas last week sold twice at that level.
However, traders said the pressure remained on the downside for the crude, in the face of West African imports.
--Singapore Newsroom (+65 870 3081)
